decisive_items: A metal artifact reduction sequence MRI revealed a left periprosthetic soft‐tissue mass measuring 9 × 8 × 10 cm, without bony involvement or bone‐marrow edema.
Hip aspiration yielded 10,750 white cells/μL; all cultures were negative.
Serum cobalt and chromium levels were within normal limits.
response.rationale: Large periprosthetic soft-tissue mass without infection (negative cultures) or bursitis (no response to injection) points to ALTR; normal metal ions do not exclude it, and ceramic-on-ceramic can also cause ALTR. Infection is less likely due to negative cultures and mild inflammatory markers.

rejected.why: Initial bursitis diagnosis and partial relief are outweighed by progressive symptoms and a large MRI mass, which is not typical of simple bursitis.
Elevated WBC count is suggestive, but negative cultures and lack of systemic symptoms make infection less likely than ALTR.
